UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2876 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 19.03.2021 
 
COMMUNICATION MECHANISM TO CREATE AWARENESS 
 
2876     SHRI SURENDRA SINGH NAGAR: 
  
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be 
pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government is planning to bring in any commu
 nication mechanism to 
be adopted at various levels to create awareness about need for skill development at 
local, State, district and village levels; 
 
(b) whether Government is considering to adopt State Skill Development Mission 
(SSD
M) to organize advertisement campaigns in local language through electronic 
and print media; 
 
(c) whether any steps are being taken at school level to create awareness about 
voca
tional education, apprenticeship, etc., if so, details thereof; and 
 
(d) whether Government has entered into any partnership with international 
agencies for vocational training opportunities and if so, details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF  
SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a):  The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) periodically 
engages with the media and does advocacy with regard to skill development and its 
relevance to the current market demand, through Rojgar Melas, Kaushal Mahotsav, 
counselling sessions for youth, interactive sessions and activities, panel discussions, 
Kushal Yuva Samvaad  and also through events to celebrate their success, 
achievements and milestones.  Success case studies of students who have been 
able to transform their lives through skill development are also propagated to inspire 
others to hone a skill of their choice.  
 
A central repository is maintained by the Ministry which enables the flow of 
information regarding schemes, programs, events and initiatives. Government 
channels, events, platforms, symposiums and webinars are also utilized to 
communicate skill development initiatives and activities. Partnerships in the field of 
skilling with other Central Ministries, States, Corporate, Academia, etc. are also 
promoted with the help of offline and online media. Extensive social media outreach 
is done with periodic on-ground activation to widen the reach of skill development in 
the country. Further, various organizations under the Ministry like the National Skill 
Development Corporation (NSDC), Directorate General of Training, National Institute 
514

for Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development (NIESBUD) and Indian 
Institute of Entrepreneurship (IIE) create awareness at their respective levels.   
(b):  The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 3.0, launched on 
15.01.2021, is focused on making skill development more demand-driven and 
decentralized in its approach, in order to empower the youth with new-age skills and 
to enhance their employability. The scheme is being implemented with the State and 
District authorities working through the State Skill Development Missions (SSDMs) 
and the District Skill Committees (DSCs). The States have been allocated budgets 
for promotion of the scheme and given full authority to utilize the funds for adopting 
the communication outreach, which works best at local level. 
 
(c):  The Department of School Education and Literacy under the Ministry of 
Education is implementing the scheme of Vocationalisation of School Education 
under the umbrella of ‘Samagra Shiksha - an integrated scheme for school 
education’, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme. The Scheme seeks to integrate 
vocational education with general academic education with an aim to prepare 
educated, employable and competitive human resource for various sectors of the 
economy. Vocational courses are taught to the students of class 9 th to 12 th who opt 
for 
vocational subject in the schools covered under the scheme. Vocational 
Education has been approved in 12,854 Secondary and Senior Secondary Schools 
under the Scheme. Further, the Central Board of Secondary Education offers 
vocational courses at secondary and senior secondary levels in its affiliated schools. 
The National Institute of Open Schooling also runs vocational courses up to higher 
secondary level. In order to create awareness, the State Governments concerned 
organizes media publicity from time to time as per need. In addition, experimential 
learning in schools, being undertaken by NSDC through short training modules, 
industry visits, apprenticeships ( Internshala), and guest speakers from industry, also 
helps in creating awareness. 
 
(d):   MSDE is implementing a program titled, Skill Acquisition and Knowledge 
Awareness for Livelihood Promotion (SANKALP), with partial loan assistance taken 
by the Government of India from the World Bank. The program is aimed at improving 
short-term skill training qualitatively and quantitatively by strengthening institutions, 
bringing in better market connectivity and inclusion of marginalized sections of the 
society. Workshops under the SANKALP program are being done to acquaint 
stakeholders at the district level with the nuances of skill development. In addition, 
the Government of India has been actively engaging with other countries including 
Japan, United Arab Emirates and Switzerland, aimed at knowledge sharing, capacity 
building for the Indian Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) 
system, and facilitating international workforce mobility of skilled and certified Indian 
workers.

state: 
 
a. whether it is a fact that the Ministry has launched a two year Mahatma Gandhi National

owship Certificate Programme in Public Policy and Management in collaboration with nine 
Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs); 
 
b. if so, the details thereof; 
 
c. the aim of the Ministry in launching this programme and how many fellowships will be awarded; 
and; 
 
d. t
he post certification avenues available to the fellows and whether Government plans to induct 
them as
 professional interns/consultants within the State/district level organizational setup?

 MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF

 DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP

(a) and (b)      Yes, the Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship (MSDE) under its World 
Bank Loan assisted Skills Acquisition and Knowledge Awareness for Livelihood Promotion 
(SANKALP) scheme has launched the phase-I of two year Mahatma Gandhi National Fellowship 
(MGNF) Programme on 08.03.2020 with IIM Bangalore as the Academic partner. Currently, under 
Phase-I 
of the MGNF Programme, 69 Fellows are deployed in 69 Districts across six States namely 
Gujarat, Karnataka, Meghalaya, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh.  Further, the National 
roll-ou
t (Phase-II) of MGNF programme to cover all Districts (excluding the Districts already cover ed 
under Phase-I of MGNF) across the country has also been launched for which the advertisement 
was released on 13.02.2021. MSDE has onboarded 9 IIMs namely, IIM Bangalore,
  IIM Ahmedabad, 
IIM Lucknow, IIM Kozhikode, IIM Visakhapatnam, IIM-Udaipur, IIM Nagpur, IIM Ranchi and IIM-

The eligibility criteria prescribed for being a Mahatma Gandhi National Fellow are as under: 
 
i. The candidate should possess a minimum qualification of a graduate degree from a 
recogni
zed University; 
ii. The candidate should be a citizen of India

iv. The candidate should possess Proficiency in official language of State of fieldwork

Rs. 50
,000 per month in first year and Rs. 60,000 per month in second year. Upon completion of

host IIM. 
 
(c)        One of the key challenges identified in the skilling ecosystem is non-availability of 
knowledgea
ble individuals for implementation of various skill development programmes especially 
at District levels. To address this gap, MGNF programme has been launched by MSDE which 
combines classroom sessions at selected Indian Institute for Managements (IIMs) with an intensive 
field immersion at the District level to strengthen the District Skill Committees (DSCs). The District 
Collector
 being the Chairperson of the District Skill Committee is the nodal person to reap the 
benefits of the MGNF in the district skilling ecosystem. The MGNF Programme has been designed 
to cover all the districts across the Country, hence the fellowships to be awarded would be more

IMPACT OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT COURSES 
 
2878  SHRI AYODHYA RAMI REDDY: 
 
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be 
pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether any study has been conducted to asses the impact of skill 
development courses on the employability of people and the difference skill 
development has made to the people who got skilled, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b)  whether there is any scheme through which people without any formal 
education but with skills in various fields are provided with skill certificates after 
proper assessment; 
 
(c)  the total number of skill development centres in the country ; and 
 
(d)  the measures taken by the Central Government to further popularise the skill 
development programmes? 
 
 
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a)  Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) is the flagship scheme of the 
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), being implemented 
through the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC). PMKVY provides for 
skill training mainly through Short-Term Training (STT) and Recognition of Prior 
Learning (RPL). PMKVY has been launched in three phases viz. PMKVY 1.0 (2015-
16), PMKVY 2.0 (2016-2020) and PMKVY 3.0, which was launched on 15.01.2021. 
NSDC had engaged Sambodhi Research and Communications to conduct a third-
party evaluation Study of PMKVY 2.0 to assess the impact of the program on the 
employability and income of its participants or beneficiaries in a holistic manner. The 
Sambodhi Study found that the mean monthly income of individuals trained and 
certified under PMKVY 2.0 – STT was 15 percent higher when compared to a 
comparison group of individuals who has not participated in PMKVY. Further, the 
average monthly income of RPL-certified individuals was found to be 19 percent 
higher than that of a comparison group of non-RPL certified individuals. 
 
(b)  The RPL component of PMKVY, which recognizes existing skills through 
orientation, and Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme of the Ministry do not 
mandate any formal education before undertaking training/ orientation in short-term 
skilling. Certification is done after completion of assessment. 
 
517

(c) Under PMKVY, training is imparted through empanelled Training Centres 
(TCs) and Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras (PMKKs). As on 19.01.2021, 14,353 
TCs have been empanelled and 738 PMKKs established. Further, 229 Jan Shikshan 
Sansthans are functional in 25 States and 3 Union Territories. In the long-term 
training eco-system, there are 14,813 Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) functioning 
in the country as of 10.03.2021.  
 
(d) The various steps taken by the Ministry to popularise the skill development 
programmes, inter-alia, include the following: 
  
o MSDE has allocated adequate funds to State Skill Development Missions 
(SSDMs) under PMKVY 3.0 for promotion of the scheme and has given full 
authority to utilize the funds for adopting the communication outreach, which 
works best at local level.  
 
o MSDE engages periodically with the media and does advocacy with regard to 
skill development and its relevance to the current market demand, through 
Rozgar Melas , Kaushal Mahotsav , and counseling sessions for youth, 
interactive sessions and activities, panel discussions, Kushal Yuva Samvaad  
and also through events to celebrate their success, achievements and 
milestones. 
 
o MSDE, through the NSDC, organizes skill competitions such as IndiaSkills 
which are conducted across state, regional and national levels to make skills 
aspirational for youth.   
 
o Further, various organizations under the aegis of MSDE viz. NSDC, 
Directorate General of Training, Indian Institute of Entrepreneurship, and 
National Institute of Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development 
(NIESBUD) also create awareness at their respective levels.

Will
 the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURS HIP be

(a) the number of youngsters that got jobs through the s chemes run by the 
Ministry; 
 
(b) whether the Ministry has a facility for providing jobs geographical and sector-
wise; and  
 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
    
(a) to (c) The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) is 
implementing a number of schemes to impart employable skills to people belonging 
to different geographies, sectors and strata of the population. The Ministry is 
implementing Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan 
Sansthan (JSS) Scheme and National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) for 
short-term skill training in various sectors and Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) 
through the Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) for long-term training. Under the Short-
Term Training component of PMKVY 2.0 (2016-2020), as on 19.01.2021, 18.95 lakh 
candidates have been reported placed in jobs under various sectors. Recognition of 
Prior Learning Component of PMKVY, JSS, NAPS and CTS do not have placement 
as a criteria. Further, the Ministry through the National Skill Development Corporation 
has launched the Aatmanirbhar Skilled Employee Employer Mapping (ASEEM) portal 
to help skilled people find sustainable livelihood opportunities. As on 05.03.2021, 
1.29 crore skilled personnel have been on-boarded on the portal and around 8.4 lakh 
job offers have been made.

2880  DR. SASMIT PATRA:  
  
           Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the evidence that shows there has been growth in entrepreneurship in India; 
 
(b) the challenges faced in developing entrepreneurship in India;  and 
 
(c
)    the reasons for high levels of unemployment persisting despite efforts to improve 
entrepren
eurship in India? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI R. K. SINGH) 
(a):   According to Economic Survey 2019-2020, India ranks third in number of new firms 
created and the new firm creation has gone up dramatically in India since 2014. While the 
number of new firms in the formal sector grew at a cumulative annual growth rate of 3.8 per 
cent from 2006-2014, the growth rate from 2014 to 2018 has been 12.2 per cent. As a result, 
from about 70,000 new firms created in 2014, the number has grown by about 80 per cent to 
about 1,24,000 new firms in 2018.       
  
(b):   Some of the challenges faced by entrepreneurs in Micro, Small and Medium (MSME) 
sector, as categorized  by the ‘Expert Committee on Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises’ 
constituted by Reserve Bank of India(June 2019),  are lack of formalization, lack of timely 
payments to MSMEs, absence of backward and forward infrastructural linkages, lack of 
access to formal credit & equity support, limited access to market, information 
asymmetry, lack of managerial, legal and technical know how, etc. 
  
(c):    As per the Annual Periodic Labour  Force Survey (PLFS) for 2017-18 and 2018-19 
done by National Statistical Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme 
Implementation, the estimated unemployment rate (state-wise) to the extent available for 
persons of all ages on usual status (principal status + subsidiary status) basis in the country, 
is given at Annexure-I. Thus, it is seen that the unemployment in the country has gone 
down from 6.1% in 2017-18 to 5.8% in 2018-19.

(क)  मंत्रालय द्वारा छोटे नर्क्र े ताओं, नर्शेषत: सूक्ष् म, लघ ु और मध् यम उद्यम ्ेत्र क े  नर्क्र े ताओं को पपिे 
उत् पादों क का लिला ि नर्क्रय करिे में सहायता दों ेिे क े  नलक ‍ या कदों म उ ाक गक हैं;

   ‍ यौरा ‍ या है;

ञानाि में यह बात    है नक  - र्ानणज् य उपभो‍ ताओं क े  पास पपि  नशकायत दों जव

, तो उपभो‍ ताओं की नशकायतक क े  निर्ारण में िक नियम नकस प्रकार सहायक हकगे ?

(श्री िाावल रावसाहलब िािाराव) 
 
(क) से (ग):  उद्योग सं
र् वि और  ंतररक व् यापार नर्भाग (ल प     ट ) िे भौगोनलक पर्नस् नत 
(ज   ) उत् पादों क, नखलौिक क े  लघ ु नर्क्र े ताओं को लि बोनलिंग क े  नलक नर्नभन् ि  -र्ानणज् य ्‍ लेटराम  क े  सा

की है।  सक े  पनतरर‍ त , ेसे उत् पादों क की श्‍ यता ब़ाािे क े  नलक ेसे उत् पादों क क े  नलक पृ क खोज स ुनर् ा प्रदों ाि 
करिे और उिक े  ्‍ लेटराम  पर  ि उत् पादों क को शोक े स करिे हेत ु कक स् टोररंटं ट नर्कनसत करिे क े  नलक  -र्ानणज् य 
्‍ लेटरामव नियु‍ त नकक गक हैं।

2812. श्री सैयद जफर इस् लाम:  
क्या खाद्य प्रसांस् िरण उद्यरग मांत्ी यह बताने की क ृ पा करेंगे लक:  
(ि)  क्या सरकार ने उत् तर प्रदेश क े  ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में क ृ लि- उत् पादों क े  प्रसंस् करण क े  ललए कोई 
दीर्चकाललक योजना तैयार की है; और   
(ख)  यलद हां, तो इस संबंध में ब् यौरा क् या है? 
 
उत्तर  
खाद्य प्रसांस्करण उद्यरग राज्य मांत्ी 
(श्री रामेश्वर तेली) 
 
(ि) से (ख) खाद्य प्रसंस् करण उद्योग मंत्रालय (एमओएफपीआई) क ें द्रीय क्षेत्र की एक अम्‍ब रैला 
स् कीम – प्रधान मंत्री लकसान सम्‍ब पदा योजना (पीएमक े एसवाई) को क ृ लि उत् पाद प्रसंस् करण सलहत खाद्य 
प्रसंस् करण क्षेत्र की समग्र वृद्धि एवं लवकास हेतु कायाचद्धित कर रहा है । इस स् कीम में विच 2016-17 से 
2019-20 की अवलध क े  ललए 6,000 करोड़ रुपए का पररव् यय है । इस अवलध को लवत् त विच 2020-21 
तक बढा लदया गया है । पीएमक े एसवाई की र्टक स् कीमें हैं-  (i) मेगा फ ू ड पाक च, (ii) एकीक ृ त शीत 
श्ृंखला एवं मूल् यवधचन अवसंरर्ना, (iii) खाद्य प्रसंस् करण एवं परररक्षण क्षमता सृजन/लवस् तार (iv) क ृ लि-
प्रसंस् करण क् लस् टर अवसंरर्ना, (v) बैकवडच एवं फारवडच ललंक े ज सृजन (vi) खाद्य संरक्षा एवं गुणवत् ता 
आश् वासन अवसंरर्ना, (vii) मानव संसाधन एवं संस् थान, (viii) ऑपरेशन ग्रीन् स ।  
 पीएमक े एसवाई की र्टक स् कीमों में एमओएफपीआई अलधकांशत:  उद्यलमयों को खाद्य 
प्रसंस् करण/परररक्षण उद्योग स् थालपत करने क े  ललए क्रेलडट ललंक् ड लवत् तीय सहायता (प्रारंलभक पूंजी) 
अनुदान सहायता क े  रूप में प्रदान करती है । पीएमक े एसवाई कोई क्षेत्र या राज् य लवलशष् ट नहीं हैं परंतु, 
मांग आधाररत है और इसे उत् तर प्रदेश क े  ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों सलहत पूरे देश में कायाचद्धित लकया जाता है । 
अभी तक मंत्रालय ने उत् तर प्रदेश में पीएमक े एसवाई की संगत र्टक योजनाओं में 23 कोल् ड र्ेन 
पररयोजनाए ं, 3 क ृ लि-प्रसंस् करण क् लस् टर, 22 खाद्य प्रसंस् करण यूलनटें, 6 बैकवडच एवं फारवडच ललंक े  
सृजन पररयोजनाए ं  और 9 खाद्य परीक्षण प्रयोगशाला पररयोजनाए ं  अनुमोलदत की है ।  
आत्म लनभचर भारत पहल क े  भाग क े  रूप में एमओएफपीआई 2020-21 से 2024 -25 तक 
पांर् विों क े  दौरान क्र े लडट ललंक्ड सद्धिडी क े  माध्यम से 2 लाख  सूक्ष् म खाद्य प्रसंस् करण उद्यमों की 
स्थापना/उन्नयन क े  ललए लवत्तीय, तकनीकी और व्यावसालयक सहायता प्रदान करने क े  ललए क ें द्र 
प्रायोलजत स् कीम-प्रधानमंत्री सूक्ष् म खाद्य प्रसंस् करण उद्यम उन् नयन (पीएमएफएमई) योजना को 10,000 
करोड़ रुपए क े  पररव् यय क े  साथ कायाचद्धन् वत कर रहा है ।  इसमें से उत् तर प्रदेश को अगले पांर् विों क े  
ललए 1731.60करोड़ रुपये क े  पररव्यय क े  साथ क ु ल 37826 यूलनटें आवंलटत की गई हैं।

19 मार्च, 2021 को उत्तर देने क े  ललए 
 
पीएमएफएमई ि े  अांतर्गत िार्ागन् वर्न  
2814   श्री मो. नदीमुल हि:  
 डा.नरेन् र जाधव:  
क्या खाद्य प्रसांस् िरण उद्योर् मांत्री यह बताने की क ृ पा करेंगे लक:  
(ि)  प्रधानमंत्री सूक्ष् म खाद्य उद्योग उन् नयन योजना (पीएमएफएमई) क े  अंतगचत लकतने लकसान उत् पादक संगठन 
स् वयं सेवी समूह और उत् पादक सहकारी संस् थाऍं  लाभान्न् वत हुई हैं, इसका राज् य-वार ब् यौरा क् या है;  
(ख)  इस योजना क े  अंतगचत उन् नयन क े  ललए लकतने मौजूदा सूक्ष् म खाद्य प्रसंस् करण उद्योगों को लवत् तीय, प्रौद्योलगकीय 
और व् यापाररक सहायता प्रदान की गई है, प्रदान की गई सहायता का राज् य-वार ब् यौरा क् या है;   
(र्)  योजना क े  अंतगचत कौशल प्रलशक्षण, खाद्य सुरक्षा, मानकों और स् वच् छता संबंधी तकनीकी ज्ञान प्रदान करने तथा 
गुणवत् ता सुधार क े  ललए अब तक कौन-कौन से क्षमता लनमाचण उपाय लकये गये हैं; और  
(घ) योजना क े  अंतगचत राज् य-वार आंवलित लनलध का लकतना उपयोग लकया गया है?    
 
उत्तर 
 
खाद्य प्रसांस्करण उद्योर् राज्य मांत्री 
(श्री रामेश्वर तेली) 
 
(ि) और (ख):  पीएमएफएमई स् कीम को मंलत्रमंडल द्वारा मई, 2020 में अनुमोलदत लकया गया था और स् कीम क े  
लदशालनदेशों को जून 2020 में जारी लकया गया था । मंत्रालय ने व् यन्िगत सूक्ष् म खाद्य प्रसंस् करण उद्यमों से आवेदन 
प्रस् तुत करने क े  ललए एमआईएस पोिचल का शुभारंभ 25 जनवरी, 2021 को लकया था । 16 मार्च, 2021 की न्स्थलत क े  
अनुसार 1534 आवेदन प्रस् तुत लकए गए हैं । लडन्र ि क ररसोसच पसचन/ लडन्र ि क लेवल कमेिी संबंलधत राज् यों/संघ शालसत 
क्षेत्रों में आवेदनों की जांर् कर रही है ।  
समूह अथाचत एसएर्जीज, एफपीओज और सहकाररताओं क े ललए पूंजी लनवेश क े  ललए ऑनलाइन आवेदन 
मॉड्यूल लवकास क े  र्रण क े  अंतगचत है । ऑफलाइन आवेदनों को 07 जनवरी, 2021 से आमंलत्रत लकया गया है । प्रस् तुत 
आवेदनों/अनुमोलदत क े  लववरणों को राज् यों और संघ शालसत क्षेत्रों द्वारा अभी अंलतम रूप लदया जाना है ।  
करीब 40,000 एसएर्जीज सदस् य जो खाद्य प्रसंस् करण में शालमल  हैं की एसआरएलएम द्वारा प्रारंलभक पूंजी क े  
ललए पहर्ान की गई है । एसआरएलएम एसएर्जीज सदस् यों क े  लववरणों की जांर्/प्रमाणन कर रहा है । स् कीम क े  
लदशालनदेशों क े  अनुसार एसएर्जीज सदस् यों को एसआरएलएम की लसफाररश क े  आधार पर प्रारंलभक पूंजी क े  ललए 
समथचन उपलब् ध कराया जाएगा ।  
(र्): अभी तक स् कीम क े  अंतगचत लनम् नललन्खत क्षमता लनमाचण उपायों को आरंभ लकया गया है:- 
i. क्षमता लनमाचण पर लवस् तृत लदशालनदेशों को नवम् बर, 2020 में जारी लकया गया था ।   
ii. 35 राज् यों/संघ शालसत क्षेत्रों क े  राज् य स् तर तकनीकी संस् थानों (एसएलिीआई) को मंत्रालय द्वारा अनुमोलदत 
लकया गया है ।  
iii. 334 मास् िर ि िेनरों का प्रलशक्षण ईडीपी और लवलभन् न खाद्य उत् पादों पर आयोलजत लकया गया ।  
iv. 9 राज् यों में 177 लजला स् तर क े  ि िेनरों को प्रलशलक्षत लकया गया ।  
v. लनफ्टेम और आईआईएफपीिी ने ि िेलनंग मॉड्यूल (ओडीओपी) तैयार लकए हैं जो एमओएफपीआई, लनफ्टेम 
और आईआईएफपीिी की वेबसाइिों पर प्र कालशत लकए गए    हैं ।  
(घ): स् कीम क े  अंतगचत राज् य और संघ शालसत क्षेत्र-वार जारी लनलधयों का लववरण सांलग् नि में लदया गया है  ।

 (ग): पाक च  में स्थालपत की जाने िाली प्रमुख सामान्य सुलिधाओं की क्षमता में िेयरहाउस-4000 मीलर् ि क र्न, कोल्ड

संचालन प्रकिया (एसओपी) आदि पंचायतों को उपलब्ध कराए गए हैं। ये ई -ग्राम स्वराज वेबसाइट 
(https://egramswaraj.gov.in/) पर भी उपलब्ध हैं।  
 
पंचायतों को क ें रीय ववि आयोग के तहत प्रिान की गई ननधध पर नज़र रखने और सेवा प्रिाताओं को  
वास्तववक समय पर भुगतान करने के र्लए ई -ग्राम स्वराज को सावचजननक वविीय प्रबंधन प्रणाली 
(पीएफएमएस) के सार् एकीक ृत ककया गया है , श्जसे ई-ग्राम स्वराज-पीएफएमएस इंटरफ े स 
(ईजीएसपीआई) कहा जाता है। ईजीएसपीआई सुदृढ़ वविीय प्रबंधन प्रणाली स्र्ावपत करने, पंचायतों की 
पारिर्शचता और जवाबिेही बढ़ाने की पररकल्पना करता है। 
 
अभी तक वर्च 2020-21 के र्लए 2.47 लाख ग्राम पंचायतें (जीपी) और वर्च 2021-22 के र्लए 1.58  
लाख ग्राम पंचायतों ने अपनी ग्राम पंचायत ववकास योजनाओं (जीपीिीपी) को तैयार और अपलोि ककया 
है। 2.35 लाख ग्राम पंचायतों ने वर्च 2019-20 के र्लए अपनी ईयर ब ुक बंि कर िी हैं और 1.92 लाख 
ग्राम पंचायतों ने 2020-21 के र्लए मंर् बुक बंि कर िी हैं। इसके अलावा , 14 वें ववि आयोग के तहत  
1.03 लाख ग्राम पंचायतों और 1.43 लाख ग्राम पंचायतों ने िमशिः वर्च 2019-20 और वर्च 2020-21 के 
िौरान ऑनलाइन लेनिेन ककया है। इ स प्रकार 1.08 लाख ग्राम पंचायतों ने चाल ू वर्च में पंरहवें ववि 
आयोग के तहत ऑनलाइन लेन -िेन ककया है। मंत्रालय ई-ग्राम स्वराज अन ुप्रयोग के लगातार सुधार के

REFERENCE BY THE CHAIR 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, today, i.e. , 22nd March, is the World Water Day, a 
day that is observed to advocate sustainable management of fresh water resources. 
This year, the United Nation’s theme for ‘World Water Day’ is ‘Valuing Water’ which 
highlights the value of water going beyond its mere numerical price. Water has 
enormous and complex value for our households, food, culture, health, education, 
economics and integrity of our natural environment. By overlooking these multi -
dimensional values, we risk mismanaging this finite, irreplaceable resource and will be 
unable to save it for the benefit of everyone and for generations to come. 
…(Interruptions)…Please, Mr. Sanjay, some observation is being made by the Chair, 
so, nothing should be there, you can do it later; no problem. With the ever- growing 
population, the demand for water has increased manifold, fulfilment of which is 
already putting enormous pressure on our limited natural resources and is eventually 
degrading the environment. The situation has further been exacerbated by the 
reckless exploitation and imprudent consumption of water. Conservation of water and 
preservation of our water resources is of utmost importance for our country, given the 
fact that our country has 16 per cent of the global population, but, only 4 per cent of 
the world's fresh water.  
Almost all civilizations had flourished on the banks of rivers indicating how vital 
water is for our survival.  For us Indians, water is an intrinsic part of our lives and 
ceremonies from birth to death. We revere rivers as our mothers. The many Vedic 
hymns like ‘Nadi Sukta’ and ‘Apah Suktam’ from Rig Veda invoking 'Water' as the 
bestower of vigour and strength, the nurturer of farmlands, the refreshing presence 
and the cleanser of both body and spirit, stand testimony to our close associatio n 
with water. We need to carry this legacy forward by preserving and nurturing our 
rivers and freshwater resources like lakes, ponds, etc.  
In line with this year's theme for 'World Water Day', we also need to 
acknowledge and at the same time develop an active consciousness for the  multi-
dimensional value that water holds for us as it will help us develop a holistic and 
integrated perspective on water conservation.  

2 [RAJYA SABHA] 
 
As parliamentarians, it is our bounden duty to act as role models and 
trailblazers in water conservation, by adopting sustainable water management 
practices both in personal and public life and sensitize one and all in inculcating water 
conservation techniques like rain water harvesting, afforestation of river banks to 
prevent soil erosion and reduce annual rainwater runoff.  
I hope the entire House will join me in supporting the conservation of water 
resources and ensuring judicious use of water so that while fulfilling our needs, 
enough is left for our future generations.  
MR. C HAIRMAN: I have one appeal to all, whatever you want to talk, you can 
complete it before entering into the House and whatever you have to talk in the 
House, i.e., on subjects where you are permitted, that can be performed here. Other 
responsibilities can b e performed in the Lobbies; the Lobbies are meant for that 
purpose also. So, keep that in mind and particularly when the Chair is making some 
observation, it is not fair on the part of anybody to disturb the other man, when he is 
keenly hearing the observation, is not a good thing to follow; please keep this advice 
in mind.

*272. SHRIMATI CHHAYA VERMA: Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST 
AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is aware of the fact that wild animals roaming outside the 
forest are causing harm to farmers’ crops; 
(b) whether Government has developed any mechanism to compe nsate for the 
loss caused by wild animals/ live stocks, in view of their increasing population in 
forest; 
(c) the ex-gratia amount released under the schemes sponsored by Central 
Government for the compensation of the loss to the crops due to animal nuisan ce in 
last three years; and  
(d) whether Government is proposing to control the population of wild animals by 
applying birth control measures on them so that the crops destruction may be 
reduced? 
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE (SHRI  
PRAKASH JAVADEKAR):  (a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 

58 [RAJYA SABHA] 
 
Statement 
(a) As a result of concerted efforts made for protection and conservation of 
wildlife, the population of several wildlife species like Tigers, Elephants, Asiatic Lion, 
Rhino etc. in the country has increased. There are reports of wild animals moving out 
of the forests leading to human wildlife conflict situations including crop damage. The 
Ministry is implementing Centrally Sponsored Schemes –  ‘Development of Wildlife 
Habitat’, ‘Project Elephant’ and ‘Project Tiger’ which inter -alia aim to improve the 
natural habitat of wild animals so as to minimize their movement to human 
habitations. Further, improvement of degraded forests and augmentation of fodder 
and water are major components for use of Compensatory Afforestation Fund 
available with States/UTs. These components also help in improving natural habitats 
of wild animals and preventing their movement to human habitations. 
(b)   The compensation mechanisms for the crop dam age due to wild animals             
vary from State to State. The Ministry provides financial assistance to the States/UTs 
under the Centrally Sponsored Schemes –  ‘Development of Wildlife Habitat’ and 
‘Project Elephant’, which also include assistance for p ayment of compensation for 
loss of crops due to damage by wild animals. 
Further, the Ministry has increased the ex -gratia payment in connection with 
wildlife depredation. 
Under the revamped operational guidelines of Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima 
Yojna (PMFBY), issued by the Government of India (effective from the year 2020), 
States can provide add-on coverage for crop loss due to attack by wild animals. 
(c) During the last three years, ex -gratia amount of Rs. 1,777.915 lakhs were  
released under the Cent rally Sponsored Scheme ‘Project Elephant’ and Rs. 478.40 
lakhs under ‘Development of Wildlife Habitats’ scheme, to the States. 
(d) Ministry has sanctioned a project for immuno -contraception to control birth of 
wild animals to Wildlife Institute of India, D ehradun and National Institute of 
Immunology, New Delhi. The project envisages using contraceptives to control 
populations of Rhesus macaque, Nilgai, Wild pig and elephants. The objective of the 
project is to develop appropriate methods for population cont rol of above species in 
select sites, to reduce human wildlife conflict.

R. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, today, i.e., 22 nd March, is the World Water Day, a 
day that is observed to advocate sustainable management of fresh water resources. 
This year, the United Nation’s theme for ‘World Water Day’ is ‘Valuing Water’ which 
highlights the value of water going bey ond its mere numerical price. Water has 
enormous and complex value for our households, food, culture, health, education, 
economics and integrity of our natural environment. By overlooking these multi -
dimensional values, we risk mismanaging this finite, irreplaceable resource and will be 
unable to save it for the benefit of everyone and for generations to come. 
…(Interruptions)…  Please, Mr. Sanjay, some observation is being made by the Chair, 
so, nothing should be there, you can do it later; no problem. With the ever- growing 
population, the demand for water has increased manifold, fulfilment of which is 
already putting enormous pressure on our limited natural resources and is eventually 
degrading the environment. The situation has further been exacerbated by  the 
reckless exploitation and imprudent consumption of water. Conservation of water and 
preservation of our water resources is of utmost importance for our country, given the 
fact that our country has 16 per cent of the global population, but, only 4 per cent of 
the world's fresh water.  
Almost all civilizations had flourished on the banks of rivers indicating how vital 
water is for our survival.  For us Indians, water is an intrinsic part of our lives and 
ceremonies from birth to death. We revere rivers as our mothers. The many Vedic 
hymns like ‘Nadi Sukta’ and ‘Apah Suktam’ from Rig Veda invoking 'Water' as the 
bestower of vigour and strength, the nurturer of farmlands, the refreshing presence 
and the cleanser of both body and spirit, stand testimony to o ur close association 
with water. We need to carry this legacy forward by preserving and nurturing our 
rivers and freshwater resources like lakes, ponds, etc.  
In line with this year's theme for 'World Water Day', we also need to 
acknowledge and at the same time develop an active consciousness for the  multi -
dimensional value that water holds for us as it will help us develop a holistic and 

integrated perspective on water conservation. 
As parliamentarians, it is our bounden duty to act as role models and 
trailblazers in water conservation, by adopting sustainable water management 
practices both in personal and public life and sensitize one and all in inculcating water 
conservation techniques like rain water harvesting, afforestation of river banks to 
prevent soil erosion and reduce annual rainwater runoff.  
I hope the entire House will join me in supporting the conservation of water 
resources and ensuring judicious use of water so that while fulfilling our needs, 
enough is left for our future generations.

Need for strengthening cyber security 
 
DR. NARENDRA JADHAV  (Nominated):  Mr. Chairman, Sir, I thank you for this 
opportunity to speak.  Sir, I would like to invite the attention of this august House to a 
very serious problem. Cyber terrorism or cyber attacks on critical informational 
infrastructure is a matter of grave concern.  Critical information infrastructure typically 
includes those facilities, those systems, those functions, whose incapacity or 
destruction can weaken the national security, governance, economy and overall well -
being of the country. Sir, cyber attacks on CII  can lead to huge financial loss, can 
cause huge environmental damage and pose a threat to defence security and integrity 
of the country.  
 Sir, the recent cyber attacks on Mumbai's power grid is a reminder of the 
vulnerability of India's key installations. As reported in the international media, a 
hacker group called Red Echo --one can guess the country of its origin --has 
repeatedly targeted the control rooms of Power System Operation Corporation 
Limited. The Maharashtra Government Cyber Police have found evidence of Trojan 
infiltration of the server of the Maharashtra State Electricity Board. Reportedly, 
another hacker group--this time the name is Stone Panda; no award for guessing the 
country of origin --has recently aimed its cyber modes at Serum Institute and Bharat 
Biotech to exfiltrate intellectual property.  
 Sir, this is nothing but proxy warfare. I don't want to be an alarmist but there is 
a non -trivial possibility that this could escalate even to a nuclear plant meltdown! I 
strongly urge the Government to strengthen our cyber security demonstrably. Some 
experts say that this was just a signal. I don't want to be a jingoist. But the time has 
come to give an effective, return signal. We must demonstrate to any country which is 
threatening our national security what we are capable of.  Thank you very much, Sir.

Demand to enact a law for Health Guarantee to provide standardized healthcare 
 
DR. FAUZIA KHAN  (Maharashtra): Hon. Chairman, Sir, the responsibility to provide 
healthcare is enshrined in the Constitution. Today, however, it seems that the 
healthcare sector has become a business sector.  People are reluctant to go to 
Government-run hospitals because of the casual approach of the staff towards the 
patients in many hospitals. People go to a Government -run hospital only when they 
absolutely cannot afford treatment in a private hospital. They would prefer to sell off 
44

gold or property to go to a private hospital rather than a Government -run hospital.  
The Government should enact a health guarantee law and guarantee the provision of 
health facilities to all the people through the Government.  The criteria for health 
facilities should be decided by the Government.  It is necessary to determine SOPs for 
healthcare.  Currently, such a procedure does not exist.  The responsibility of the 
treating doctors, nurses and other staff also needs to be determined.  Moreover, 
there is a great need for transparency.  Placing the diagnosis, laboratory reports and 
reports of other tests, the time -wise treatment provided by the hospital in a place 
accessible to the relatives of the patient should be made mandatory.  This could be 
made more transparent by designing a software or using a digital method.  Healthcare 
personnel must be trained in courtesy and polite behaviour.  It would greatly reduce 
angry attacks on healthcare personnel, for which safeguards are designed by 
Governments.  Healthcare ought to be the right of every citizen.  As th is is a matter 
related to public importance, I request the Government to consider it.

Demand for the constitution of All India Judicial Services 
 
SHRI SUSHIL KUMAR MODI  (BIHAR):  Sir, in the year 1976
, Article 312 of the 
Constitution was amended by 46th Constitution Amendment for providing constitution 
of All India Judicial Service on the pattern of IAS, IPS and other All India Services.  
It may be recalled that the Law Commission's 14th Report 1958 and 116th Report 
1986, and  the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution 
Chaired by Justice H.R. Khanna, and  Justice Shri B.P. Jeevan Reddy and Shri K. 
Parasaran as members, also recommended that All India Judicial Service should be 
formed.  
Even after 
45 years of 46th Constitution Amendment, All India Judicial Service 
has not seen the light of day. Today, there is negligible representation of SCs, STs 
and OBCs in the Judiciary. We also wish that proper reservation to SCs, STs and 
OBCs be given in All India Judicial Service.  
When earlier efforts were made, there was opposition from the judiciary and
 
some raised language as a barrier for such an All  India Service. But I think language 
should not become a hindrance in such a service because IAS officers also go to 
different States and language never becomes a hurdle in their way.  
Now time has come to constitute All India Judicial Service. I urge the 
Government of India to take this initiative and take all the stakeholders into confidence 
and fulfil the demand of All India Judicial Service. Like the GST and the IBC, this will 
go down in the history as a milestone in judicial reforms.

loss caused by wild animals/ live stocks, in view of their increasing population in 
forest; 
(c) the ex -gratia amount released under the schemes sponsored by Central 
Government for the compensation of the loss to the crops due to animal nuisance in 
last three years; and  
(d) whether Government is proposing to control the population of wild animals by 
applying birth control measures on them so that the crops destruction may be 
reduced? 
 
THE M INISTER OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE (SHRI 
PRAKASH JAVADEKAR):  (a) to (d) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
 
Statement 
 
(a) As a result of concerted efforts made for protection and conservation of wildlife, 
the population of several wildlife species like Tigers, Elephants, Asiatic Lion, Rhino

[22 March, 2021]
63

 
 
etc. in the country has increased. There are reports of wild animals moving out of the  
forests leading to human wildlife conflict situations including crop damage. The 
Ministry is implementing Centrally Sponsored Schemes – ‘Development of Wildlife 
Habitat’, ‘Project Elephant’ and ‘Project Tiger’ which inter- alia aim to improve the 
natural h abitat of wild animals so as to minimize their movement to human 
habitations. Further, improvement of degraded forests and augmentation of fodder 
and water are major components for use of Compensatory Afforestation Fund 
available with States/UTs. These com ponents also help in improving natural habitats 
of wild animals and preventing their movement to human habitations. 
 
(b) The compensation mechanisms for the crop damage due to wild animals vary 
from State to State. The Ministry provides financial assistance to the States/UTs 
under the Centrally Sponsored Schemes – ‘Development of Wildlife Habitat’ and 
‘Project Elephant’, which also include assistance for payment of compensation for 
loss of crops due to damage by wild animals. 
Further, the Ministry has increased the ex -gratia payment in connection with wildlife 
depredation. 
Under the revamped operational guidelines of Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna 
(PMFBY), issued by the Government of India (effective from the year 2020), States 
can provide add-on coverage for crop loss due to attack by wild animals. 
 
(c) During the last three years, ex -gratia amount of Rs. 1,777.915 lakhs was 
released under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme ‘Project Elephant’ and Rs. 478.40 
lakhs under ‘Development of Wildlife Habitats’ scheme, to the States. 
 
(d) Ministry has sanctioned a project for immuno -contraception to control birth of 
wild animals to Wildlife Institute of India, Dehradun and National Institute of 
Immunology, New Delhi. The project envisages using contraceptives to contro l 
populations of Rhesus macaque, Nilgai, Wild pig and elephants. The objective of the 
project is to develop appropriate methods for population control of above species in 
select sites, to reduce human wildlife conflict.

SHRIMATI JHARNA DAS BAIDYA ( Tripura):  Mr. Vice-Chairman, Sir, I thank you for 
letting me speak on the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) 
Amendment Bill, 2021. 
 Sir, the key points of the Bill are:    First is the removal of restriction on end-use 
of minerals.   Second is the sale of minerals by captive mines.  Third key point relates 
to the auction by the Central Government in c ertain cases. Fourth is the transfer of 
statutory clearnace.  Fifth point is the allocation of mines with expired leases.   Sixth 
point relates to the rights of certain existing concession holders. Seventh is the 
extension of leases to Government companies. There are conditions for lapse of 
mining leases and non -exclusive reconnaissance permit. There are a few areas of 
improvement, which I would like to put forward. According to para 4(i) of the 
Statement of Objects and Reasons, the Ministry of Mines is pro posing to allow 
captive mine holders to sell up to 50 per cent of the minerals excavated during the 
current year, after meeting the requirement of the attached plant.    
 The other provision is that the captive mines, which are there, are now being 
allowed to sell 50 per cent of their produce to private parties.  That is also not good 
because the idea   of captive mines will go away totally.  So far, the State 
Governments were auctioning their mines.  Now, this amendment says that if the 
State Government delays the auction, then, the Central Government may take over 
the auction and the Central Government may also transfer the statutory clearances.   I 
will not go into all aspects of the Bill.   All I want to impress upon the Minister is that it 
is a good ide a to open up the mining sector.  But, minerals are permanent assets of 
the country. We should see that they are properly utilised for the benefit of the country 
and not for the profit of a few people. We must ensure that the tribals, who live on the 
land where the mines are being set up, are not displaced. If they are displaced, total 
rehabilitation must be promised and ensured. We must see that our minerals do not 
go away without any conversion.  
 I hope the hon. Minister would make note of these suggestions and 
incorporate them accordingly. With these words, I would say that for further 
discussion, the Bill should be sent to a select committee. Thank you.

DR. SASMIT PATRA (Odisha):  Thank you, hon. Vice Chairman, Sir, for allowing me 
to participate in discussion on this very important Bill which has great bearing on my 
mineral-rich State of Odisha. At the outset, I thank my leader and hon. Chief Minister 
Shri Naveen Patnaik for his strong and dynamic leadership in taking several innovative 
and radical measures to streamline and bring in more transparency in the mining 
sector. I take this opportunity to thank the hon. Prime Minister for allotting two mines 
for Odisha. I also thank the hon. Union Minister of Mines, Shri Pralhad Joshi ji for 
incorporating most of the recommendations sent by our Odisha Government. His 
efforts in reforming the mining sector th rough this Bill, is very praiseworthy and I 
congratulate him for that. 
My senior colleague and our Parliamentary party leader in Lok Sabha, Shri 
Pinaki Misra has already placed on record in the Lok Sabha, a couple of days back, 
the views of my party in a very descriptive and holistic manner. Since, I have a few 
minutes left; I will try to be very brief. Under the leadership of hon. Chief Minister, Shri 
Naveen Patnaik Odisha has undertaken path breaking innovations and reforms in the 
mining sector. The enact ment of OMPTS Rules, 2007 to check illegal activities in 
mineral sector, development and operationalization of i3MS software platform to 
digitise the entire gamut of transactions of the mineral sector, the introduction of 
Vehicle Tracking system to track all ore -carrying vehicles are just a few of the 
interventions that have made Odisha proud.

[MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN in the Chair.] 
 
Odisha is among the few States to have successfully conducted auction of mineral 
blocks and ensured commencement of production.   The 5T mantra of our hon. Chief 
Minister, Shri Naveen Patnaik, has become the backbone of the entire effort to 
streamline the production and despatch. Use of augmented reality technology for 
sampling grid, drone imagery for stacking evidence, modern tools and machineries 
for sampling will ensure faster sampling, analysis, transparency while safeguarding 
Government revenues.  The present set of reforms proposed by the Ministry of Mines 
are aimed at enabling the sector realise its true potential. The prospecting regime and 
exploration of mineral resources has been one of the major roadblocks facing the 
sector. The proposal to delete section 10 A (2) (b) and Section 10 A (2) (c) is a step 
in the right direction and our State Government completely agrees with this proposal. 
Similarly the proposal to allow private entities to be engaged in the exploration work is 
a very welcome step. There is no denying the fact that some of the amendments 
proposed in the Bill had been long overdue. The substituting of the words "composite 
licence" against the words "prospecting licence- cum-mining lease ” wherever they 
occur except in Clause (a) of Section 31, is a very welcome step. Similarly, redefining 
"composite licence" to mean "prospecting licence- cum-mining lease" which is a 
two-stage concession granted for the purpose of undertaking prospecting operations 
followed by mining operations in a seamless manner is likely to foster bringing in more 
number of mineral blocks to the auction fold. The proposal to substitute the words 
"production and dispatch" in place of "mining operations" in sub -section 4 of 
section 4A of the principal Act, will make the meaning of default very clear. Sir, there 
are two concerns which I would like to share with the hon. Minister and hope that he 
would clarify in his reply. Firstly, the proviso in which in cases where such auction or 
re-auction process is not completed by States within a given time, the Central 
Government may conduct auction for grant of mining lease for such area after the 
expiry of the period so specified. Another proposal is to provide the power to Central 
Government to conduct auction in cases where the State Government faces 
challenges in conduct of auction or fail to conduct auction. On this issue, we have the 
concerned and consid ered opinion that inclusions of these provisions give unbridled 
powers to the Central Government. It is, therefore, necessary that such powers are 
exercised judiciously, only in exceptional circumstances and after due consultation 
with the concerned State Government. Hon. Minister may please clarify. Another 
provision is regarding the proposed insertion of a proviso to Section 98 sub section
